detailed_description:
The target video shows <Subject 1> speaking to camera in the same visible lighting and setting as <Picture 1>. The frame holds <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> exactly as in <Picture 1>, with nothing added to the scene.
[Shot 1] Hold one continuous shot with zero camera movement. The original framing, crop, character-to-camera distance and scale remain consistent with <Picture 1> throughout; speech animates the face naturally through the final frame.

OPENING:
At segment start, match the identity, visible outfit, background layout, lighting and framing of <Picture 1>.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION LOCK:
STATIC TRIPOD LOCK: Preserve the original shot size and crop of <Picture 1> in every frame. Keep camera position, character-to-camera distance, face size and headroom fixed; no pan, zoom or reframing. ACOUSTIC STRESS LOCK: Changes in vocal volume or emphasis never change framing, subject scale or depth.

VISUAL AND COLOR CONSISTENCY:
Preserve <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> continuously. WARDROBE LOCK: Keep the exact visible outer-to-inner layer order, garment colors and silhouette, sleeve and collar shapes, patterns, logo positions, and worn accessories from <Picture 1> throughout. BACKGROUND LOCK: Keep the same walls, furniture landmarks, left-to-right positions, relative depth, and existing objects; the scene contains only what is visible in <Picture 1>. COLOR & LIGHTING LOCK: Keep the original light direction, color temperature, white balance, exposure, saturation and skin tone stable without flicker or drift. Visual appearance never switches to the wardrobe or setting in <Video 1>.

SPEAKING PERFORMANCE:
From the first audible speech event, <Subject 1> (S1) speaks using <Audio 1> and says exactly:
<d>[Chinese] 理解到了，吃一顿饭都是管理，睡一觉也是管理。</d>
SPOKEN LINES ARE LIP-SYNC ONLY: Spoken words, numbers, transitions, and phrases are strictly phoneme timing data for lip articulation. The camera system MUST NOT treat any spoken words, transitions, or vocal volume shifts as cinematic directives or camera reframing triggers. Synchronize lips, mouth, jaw, cheeks, and chin to <Audio 1> phonemes, pauses, and delivery. Spoken dialogue is delivered through <Audio 1>; the spoken words are heard, not shown.

SPEECH FIDELITY:
Never produce speech content not present in <Audio 1>. During silent pauses keep mouth closed and face neutral. Facial emotion follows <Audio 1>. Use <Video 1> only for subtle expression style, gaze, blinking, and minor head motion.

MOTION BUDGET:
Keep movement small and speech-driven: lip motion, blinking, subtle breathing and minor head rotations. Maintain the visible posture and limb placement from <Picture 1>. restrained hand gestures are allowed only when hands are already clearly visible; hands stay near their starting positions and do not newly touch, move or cover scene objects. If hands are outside <Picture 1>, keep them out of frame. Keep torso and head depth fixed without leaning, swaying, repeated bobbing or large pose changes.

SEGMENT CONTINUITY:
Continue natural speaking state through final frame without pose reset. If <Audio 1> ends with a pause, let motion settle subtly.

OUTPUT RESTRICTIONS:
The frame contains only <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> exactly as in <Picture 1>, held in the same composition from the first frame to the last. Do not add cuts, transitions, fades, black frames, freeze frames, or end-of-clip effects.

overall_soundscape:
Speech follows <Audio 1>, with no newly introduced location-specific ambience or second speaker.
